newsitem.title: USA: Cosby extortion case jurors meet again on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Cosby extortion case jurors meet again on Friday.

text.p: Jurors in the extortion trial of a woman claiming to be Bill Cosby's illegitimate daughter failed to reach a verdict on Thursday and will resume deliberations on Friday.

The jury of seven men and five women are deciding the case against Autumn Jackson, 22, who is on trial for threatening to ruin Cosby's reputation by selling her story to the Globe supermarket tabloid newpaper.
Other defendants in the case are Jose Medina, 51, and Boris Sabas, also known as Boris Shmulevich.

They are charged with conspiracy, extortion and violating the federal law that prohibits the use of interstate commerce to commit crimes. If convicted of all counts, they face a possible total prison term of 12 years and fines of $750,000.

During the trial, prosecutors had introduced as evidence recorded telephone conversations and letters in which Jackson contacted Cosby's lawyer, his publisher, CBS and Cosby's television sponsors and threatened to expose the actor as a deadbeat dad unless she received $40 million.
As part of the scheme, Jackson sent Cosby's lawyer and the former president of CBS an unsigned contract with the Globe for the sale of her story for $25,000.

On Thursday, the jury reviewed evidence that included testimony by Placido Macaraeg, who had worked with Jackson and Medina on a failed children's television show last year. Macaraeg testified about efforts by Medina and Jackson to pressure Cosby to pay the sum.
He had quoted Medina as saying, "If he (Cosby) doesn't want this to get out, he's going to have to pay a lot of money."

The jury also asked for a Jan. 16 "to do" list that was found in the Burbank, Calif. hotel room in which the defendants had worked. The list included making copies of the Globe contract and sending faxes to Cosby's lawyer and the then-president of CBS with copies to go to Cosby's sponsors.
